answer: At dawn the inlet registry opens: every agent that wants to vote or claim rewards must present a short, non-exportable hardware attestation from a physical token whose serial was burned into a glacier-cold merkle tree at issuance. Each serial can bind to only one live account; the tree rejects any second binding. An attacker who wants N independent identities must therefore buy, ship, and keep alive N separate physical tokens whose issuance fees and custody risk rise linearly with N, while honest agents pay the one-time hardware cost once.
